item.title: Re: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Wow, thank you so much! Both for the greenlight and the amazing ideas!

The backstory of the anomaly is something that I don't have completely fleshed out right now. My intention is for the anomaly to represent sudden tragedy and existential dread in this article. I do however eventually want to reveal in a future article or tale that it was no accident that the SCP landed in front of this researcher.

I had planned to just allow the researcher to be able to stop time, as I didn't want to him to be able to go back and change what happened. However, the idea of him being able to go back in time, but only messing things up further is a really interesting idea that plays into the theme. I wanted to have a theme mirroring real life where what's done is done, so I don't know if I'll incorporate this, but great suggestion.

I am planning on having a record of a Keter class containment breach with zero casualties due to the researcher stopping time and moving everyone to safety. Afterwards, he realizes the potential his powers have to help others. This, along with maybe a good word from Glass, is what convinces the foundation higher ups to not contain him like an SCP.

item.title: Ms. G. Lass
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXX has no bodily orifices and all their skin is replaced with glass. The rest of them is hollow. They were created in a glass factory explosion in Toulouse, France. They were formerly known as Georgine Lass. They were the only survivor. They have a strong hatred for transparent objects due to this, and will attempt to crack, break, or otherwise damage them when in line of sight. When exposed to even a very small amount of oxygen, they will engulf in flames reaching a temperature of 4000K. When this happens, they begin to run around erratically, usually burning though everything and everyone it comes close too.

Central Narrative: Due to the severe flammability, all methods that foundation has thus far have been found not heat resistant enough, hence ineffective. It follows the logs of a pair of containment engineers working, getting pressured, mishaps, everything, as they try to create a containment chamber capable of containing them as they posed a severe containment risk and breached containment several times. They eventually do succeed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be 2 versions of the file, 1 before the success, and 1 after. The before one will have an O5 notice stating “All Containment Engineer Personal at Site X, unless told otherwise by a Foundation Employee with Level 4 Clearance or above, must focus all research, time, and resources to the creation of a containment chamber for SCP-XXX. The budget for containment has been increased to [Large Amount Of Site’s Local Currency].”

Additional Notes: It's not just containment breaches 24/7, but more 1 monthly give or take. I will also have a recontainment procedure so it's not like it takes days to recontain.

item.title: Re: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hello!
Interesting SCP You've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So….
Wow….
I love it!
That narrative is so creative! It's such a simple concept, but you really expand on it in a way not many first-time writers do! The arc that you have would make a pretty emotional and insightful story if written correctly. My only concern is that I think the researcher would likely end up as an anomaly himself (or classified as one, at least), and may end up contained. Here are a few plotpoints I'd like to suggest

  • Does the researcher have any specific reason he connected with the anomaly? It just seems a bit random it would scan him for no reason and then just attatch to him.
  • How does he help others with the anomaly, if I may ask? Can he reverse time? Or jump forward with it? How would this help the foundation?
  • Maybe he can try to use the hourglass to go back and try to save the researchers? But maybe he ends up killing more people in the process or creating a paradox or changing reality alltogether (think "Flashpoint")
  • Perhaps using the
  • Maybe the hourglass literally breaks reality or puts the user in a loop that only he can recognize. Maybe have a repeating interview w/ Doctor glass, where each time Glass steps into the room and talks to the researcher, something is wrong.(i.e. Glass has snakes coming out of his head, the paint is the wrong color, the table is made of meatballs) And each time the researcher notices this, have the loop repeat.
  • What if the researcher went haywire? He tries locking out the guilt, and starts to think of himself as a god, reigning destruction upon the world, only for him to snap back to his senses and try to return everything to normal, only for it to break

Those are just a view ideas. But in the meantime, have a Greenlight. Best of luck on the SCP, and please let me know if you have any advice/questions/concerns about what I've said.

item.title: Re: Experience Art in a Whole New Way attempt 2
item.content:encoded:
Hello there!
Interesting SCP You've got there! Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it….

+ show block
– hide block

Overall, I'm thinking this is a relatively solid base concept, but there are a few places your concept falls flat:

  • Tropes: This concept is falling into the standard a-thing-that-does-a-thing trope, in this case, a computer that teleports people. That isn't enough to have a solid SCP. It doesn't have anything that distinguishes it from other SCPs. You need something that expands on that idea, more than just anomalous abilities. You need a story too hook your reader in and keep them there, and that's where my next point comes in.
  • Central narrative: My primary concern is that there simply isn't enough detail being put into your story, which is the most important part of the entire article. SCPs have evolved beyond simple items. You don't need to go overboard with our story. Exploration logs are a good start, but you need to go beyond that. Give me some specifics about them. Why can the computer teleport people into the images? How do the images appear? Are the images physical locations? Who goes into the painting? You mention an MTF unit, but what makes them so special? Is there a specific individual that the story revolves around?
  • Conciseness: Your story is a bit all over the place. You have an interview, a hostile group, an MTF unit, and seemingly no way that all those events are associated with each other. You want to simplify your base concept as much as possible, and then expand on the finer details. It may take a bit of thinking, but once you get that idea, you've struck gold, and the potential is endless.
  • Attention-Grabber: What is going to make your SCP different from others? Plenty of SCPs have "differing landscapes" and "recurring characters". What is different about yours? What makes yours unique? Tell me why your audience should read YOUR article, rather than another article.

Best of luck with this SCP, and please do PM me if you would like me to take another look! Great job thus far, and with a bit of effort, I think this concept is going to go a long way!

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for reply!

Key summary:

For years the SCPs have kept to themselves, away in the hills, and aren't considered much of a threat (745 is Euclid). They also behave predictably- at dusk, separate groups make multi-colored light signals to each other across the valleys.

The "Author" (1st person, unnamed) and their partner begin their overnight shift guarding the containment area, a huge tract of land. That evening, the SCPs suddenly interrupt their usual light show and conduct a different kind of display. At the same moment, radio contact is lost with one of the other security teams. Author and partner speed off in their direction to find them.

They find them safe, but discover they've joined them in a radio "dead zone." Unable to contact their base of operations, they decide to head back to their perimeter and hopefully escape the dead zone. They notice that the number of visible SCPs (points of light in the distance) are gradually increasing.

They finally get in contact with base, who confirms that they are to maintain the perimeter and await further instruction while headquarters comes up with a plan. They are also told a UAV is on the way to observe the area and provide a better idea of the situation. The number of lights continues to grow.

The UAV finally arrives, and sees what might be a lone, dim specimen separated from the group (though they're not sure what it is). The team is sent to investigate. They are apprehensive about the situation, as they feel they're under-equipped to face what might be a deadly predator, but being disciplined operators they press forward.

They gradually trek their way through the dark desert terrain, in search of… something. Author is the first to spot it- a faint light near the ground. As they move in closer, a sudden, overwhelming sounds strikes the team- a horrible shriek. It's a moment of panic and unbearable pain.

Author wakes up the next morning on the desert ground (lost time). They're picked up by a Foundation helicopter and taken to a nearby research site's clinic for treatment and recovery. Author does recall one incomplete memory from that night, a brief snapshot (I'll save that part, but if you combine it with other details from the tale, and the original file, you could draw a conclusion about what might be going on) Author is debriefed by multiple officials, but not told anything about the rest of the team or what happened with SCP-745.

At this point we learn the reason they're telling this story- they're about to undergo a procedure to attempt to recover lost time, and as part of that they have be amnesticized. They know their teammates are most likely dead or missing, and they want to save the only living memory of their last night.

item.title: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional and symbolic, with undertones of mystery and light comedic moments

Page Layout: Traditional, with an account of the recovery, and addendum containing testing logs, and a few interviews.

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious black, metal object resembling an hourglass appears in the sky above a foundation site and crashes through the roof. The object appears to consume the time of living beings near it, causing them to leap forward in time and age accordingly. The object ends up killing several researchers, but one seems to be unaffected. The object later even goes as far as to attach itself to him. This researcher then has to grapple with survivor's guilt, and must learn to keep moving forward, accepting both the good and the bad of the object being attached to him.

+ Additional Details
- Additional Details

Central Narrative: (Ultimately, I want to tell a human story about a man initially struggling with guilt, but with the help of a friend, is able to accept the way things are and work to move forward.) After crashing into a foundation site, the SCP lands near a researcher. The anomaly then proceeds to scan him. After the anomaly is contained, the research wants to learn more about it, and is appointed head researcher. During a routine examination, the SCP activates, while our main researcher and two others are in the room. The two other researchers are killed by the SCP, but our main researcher is left. Later, the SCP permanently attaches itself to him. Through interviews with Dr. Glass, we learn he is suffering with survivor’s guilt and isolation. During subsequent testing, we find out that the SCP can allow the researcher to exist outside of time. (Time stop) The end of the arc will have the researcher coming to terms with the conflict he feels towards the SCP being attached to him and using it to help the foundation/the world, while leaving the origin and purpose of the SCP open ended.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: In addition to a relatable human struggle, throughout the article, there’s hints here and there that the SCP may have been intentionally created by an unknown group.

Additional Notes: I’m hoping to expand on the backstory of the SCP in future tales or articles, as well as feature the researcher in some of my future articles. While I couldn’t explain every detail here, I have the main arc of the story pretty well thought out. Critique and greenlights welcome.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
*belatedly manifests in response to PM*

+ Updated thoughts
- on the updated post

So I'm happy to see you running with my suggestion here, for starters, and your response above shows that you're thinking in the right direction. The next thing to do here is to flesh out your description more, and start developing those ideas you mentioned. One key thing in the greenlighting process is that we're not just trying to help find and refine good ideas, but also help ya'll figure out what you're doing with the idea.

In this case, what you have currently in "Central Narrative" is really what you should have in the elevator pitch, the quick summary of what it is and what it does. Something you told me above is the start of a good central narrative, however:

It's a germaphobe because in this universe a plague was what wiped out the rest of it's species. (Man they could have really used 049.) It was the only one who could fend off the plague using it's anomalous properties.

The sole survivor of a plague trying to prevent the extinction of other species by plague is a great route to go. I'd focus on finding a clever way to communicate this story using "Show, don't tell". "Telling" would be weak narrative options like having it be able to speak and explain all this in an interview, or flatly stating in the description that the Foundation has figured all this out. "Showing" would be indirect information, observable traits, and events that together reveal all of that story in a organic, interesting way- that bit about it trying to get out of containment to clean when it overhears discussion of an illness is a good example.

A format that might work really well: a series of addenda tracing the eventful story of how this thing goes from initial containment (there's all sorts of trouble it could get into that would get the Foundation's attention…"local anti-mask protesters claim giant bug stalking them") to mostly-harmless-but-annoying containment problem to trustee member of the cleaning crew, maybe with therapy sessions for its OCD and trauma along the way.

item.title: SCP idea, looking for reviews!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch: An endless labyrinth beneath an old shack occupied by creatures that steal the physical appearances of their victims.

Central Narrative: This SCP is an old shack with boarded up windows and moss growing on it. When you enter the basement of this shack, you enter an endless labyrinth that by all accounts is impossible to escape. This labyrinth is occupied by civilians trapped inside prior to containment, and creatures that will eat you and steal your physical appearance upon getting close.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: You cannot trust anybody within the labyrinth as anybody could be one of the monsters posing as a normal human.

Additional Notes: A lot of this will be exploration logs consisting of different personnel's experiences within the labyrinth, and experiencing how the civilians within live on a day to day basis.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlights
item.content:encoded:
I had originally intended it to be kind of like the cabinet maze to where the door leads to a random area of the liminial dimension (What I have decided to dub it.) And to have creatures that were originally affected by the dimension itself to be semi-hostile creatures that would actively seek to convert others, but felt that might be too common for the wiki. I had also originally wanted it to be just normal liminial spaces that just oddly familiar despite never being there, but I needed a form of narrative and I thought that would be most fitting.
show block
Hide block

Explaining further on why it would spread, is because you can find these limnial spaces in real life. So I thought in order to do it service to have some way of reaching out of the dimension and into the regular world, which in this spread it would create things like hallways that fracticled into different areas that got steadily more warped and ragged as you went deeper. And one more point on the loss of direction, since a Liminial space, in definition is a transitional space that's in-between the past and the present, such a time anomaly I would feel would create some disorientation after awhile. Anyway, Thank you for the info and I'll definitely take it to the butterfly folks. Have a wonderful day!

item.title: The Lost City of Choris Fos (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: SCP Mission Logs & Field Tests

Elevator Pitch: A city that was discovered 12 miles out of Athens Greece that can only be seen and visited after sunset every other Sunday.

Central Narrative: The city was large part of Greek trade and power until the "Gods" judged the city leaving it cursed. Those in the city are cursed with immortality as well as being unable to leave the city. those outside have forgotten the city and it appears nowhere in any Greek history. Those in the city also seem to rely on an unlimited source of food and water and seem to receive items on a weekly schedule from what would be seen in ancient Greece.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Those who enter the city may interact and leave anytime before sunrise. Those who don't leave in time will be subjected to the same curse and will be unable to leave.

Additional Notes: The people of the city physically cannot die but can feel all the pain that would come there way via starvation, thirst, or suffering a wound.

item.content:encoded:
I am not an official critter, and I can't give greenlights.

+ Crit wants a friend
- Crit has a friend already

A shiny metal box small enough to fit in the palm of someone's hand.

So, first, anyone's hand? Does it anomalously change, or does it just stay the same?

that randomly announces the name of a random person that didn't exist until their name was announced

There's almost 8 billion people in the world. Is it a random culture, ethnicity, etc… or is it fixed? This is very vague.

If a human touches this box, it will say their full name, then proceed to sound a 60 second countdown. When the countdown stops, they will instantly become unconscious and die.

..Huh??? Why? The concept of "die when you touch it/it touches you" has probably been done 1000000 times not just on this wiki but in creepypastas in general. It's dangerous, sure, but it's very boring and plain. How would this stand out from the other 3000 dangerous SCPs that will kill you as well? It's just a box that makes a new human and kills the person that touches it. Overall, this needs a huge revision for it to be interesting.
